scope: The former Cornelius Tower in Lier as seen on 25 March 2010, including the sandstone clock front, banded brick side walls, rear canopy and slate pyramid roof with its iron finial.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The Flemish inventory describes the rectangular 1928–30 tower above its medieval base, the slate pyramid, sandstone frontage, striped brick side walls and sheltered rear stairs.
The museum records heights of 13.45 metres to the cornice, 18.38 to the chimney and 20.31 to the top of the ironwork.
